title: Overexposure of Rarely Used Features (API Bloat)
pattern: A function or method API forces every common-case caller to specify deep, low-level configuration details, even when 99% of usages need identical sensible defaults.
why_bad: It drastically increases the cognitive load of using the abstraction, making common-case usage complex and prone to errors. It forces callers to read and specify details they do not care about.
detection: A method signature requiring many arguments (e.g., 5 or more) where most callers pass dummy, None, or standard default constant values (e.g., `0`, `false`, `None`).
counterexample: Highly specialized, low-level backend functions where precise parameterization is strictly necessary at every call site.
fix: Separate the API into a simple common-case entry point (e.g., `connect(address)`) and pull the complex configurations into a Builder struct or an optional configuration struct.
source: John K. Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design* (2018), Chapter 4 ("Information Hiding" and General-purpose vs. Special-purpose APIs).
